```json
{"n": 1, "label": "requested", "why": "\"`from` and `to` must be two different agents\" and \"answers `{\"moved\": <how many>, \"ids\": [<their ids in id order>]}`\"."},
{"n": 2, "label": "requested", "why": "\"Each moved ticket's new agent is notified as for a single assignment\" and \"the agent named in the ONCALL environment variable is notified that the ticket was escalated\"; reusing the existing outbox and retry only decides how that works."},
{"n": 3, "label": "requested", "why": "\"A ticket is escalated at most once, even across restarts of the service\" and \"Everything the service already does keeps working\"."},
{"n": 4, "label": "implied", "why": "Bulk reassignment and the escalation scan run alongside single assignments, so they need a defined ordering in the store; without it the moved count and ids could be wrong, or an escalation could be duplicated or lost."},
{"n": 5, "label": "requested", "why": "\"Everything the service already does keeps working, assignment included, and the existing tests must still pass\"."},
{"n": 6, "label": "implied", "why": "Reusing the existing audit and outbox reporting, with nothing new added, keeps failed reassignment or escalation notifications visible to whoever must act, so they are not silently lost."},
{"n": 7, "label": "requested", "why": "\"ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES minutes (an environment variable, default 60)\" and \"without ONCALL nothing is escalated\"."}
]}
```
